slides.say: One pen holds x cubic centimeters of ink. To write one word, you need y cubic centimeters of ink. Hagai's pens were enough for him to write x cubed times y words. How many pens did Hagai have?
Let's try to understand it. A pen has x of ink, and a word needs y, so one pen writes x over y words. Then we'd divide x cubed y by x over y, and that's where many students get tangled.
But look at the choices. They have x and y in them, so we can plug in numbers. [short pause] We'll solve it by plugging in, and then finish the algebra.

Which numbers? The easiest would be x and y both one. But look at the choices first. They have powers, a product and fractions. With ones, every choice is one, and nothing is ruled out. So one can't tell them apart here.
at: With ones, every choice is one

slides.say: So let's take x equals two. And y? If y is two as well, x squared y squared and x cubed y are both sixteen, a tie again. Different letters, different numbers.
at: If y is two as well

slides.say: So y equals one, which keeps the story easy. Now the choices give four, eight, a quarter and an eighth. They're all different, good.
Now the story with these numbers. A pen holds two cubic centimeters, and a word needs one. So each pen writes two words.
He wrote x cubed times y words. Two cubed is eight, and eight times one is eight words. Eight words, two words a pen, so he had four pens.
at: Eight words, two words a pen

slides.say: He had four pens, so the right choice must give four. Choice number one, x squared y squared, gives four. It fits. Choice number two, x cubed y, gives eight, out. Choice numbers three and four, one over x squared y squared, and one over x cubed y, are fractions, a quarter and an eighth, out. So choice number one is our answer.
at: So choice number one is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the math way, the algebra we started. One pen writes x over y words. The number of pens is all the words, divided by the words a pen writes.
at: One pen writes x over y

slides.say: So it's x cubed y divided by x over y. Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its flip, y over x. An x cancels, so x cubed becomes x squared, and y times y is y squared. x squared y squared, choice number one again. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
